Let's denote the indefinite integral by $I=\int \frac{{ln}^{2}⁡x}{8x}\,\text{d}x.$

To use integration by parts, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={ln}^{2}⁡x & \,⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x}, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{8x} & \,⇒\,v=\int \frac{1}{8x}\text{d}x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int \frac{{ln}^{2}⁡x}{8x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({ln}^{2}⁡x)(\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{8})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{8})(\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{ln}^{3}⁡x}{8}-2\int \frac{{ln}^{2}⁡x}{8x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{ln}^{3}⁡x}{8}-2I.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for $I.$ We can ignore the constant of integration in this case, because it is insignificant for further evaluation of the definite integral.

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\frac{{ln}^{3}⁡x}{8}-2I \\ 3I & =\frac{{ln}^{3}⁡x}{8} \\ I & =\frac{{ln}^{3}⁡x}{24}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate our definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}\frac{{ln}^{2}⁡x}{8x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{24}({ln}^{3}⁡x)\,{|}_{1}^{{e}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{1}{24}({ln}^{3}⁡({e}^{3})-{ln}^{3}⁡(1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{24}((3\operatorname{ln}⁡e)^{3}-{0}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{24}({3}^{3}-0) \\  & =\frac{9}{8}\end{aligned}
$$
